records.title: What neoadjuvant therapy is for
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Neoadjuvant systemic therapy does three things that adjuvant therapy cannot. It downstages disease in the breast and the axilla, allowing less extensive surgery, better cosmesis and fewer complications such as lymphoedema, and it can render an inoperable tumour operable. It tests the biology of the tumour in vivo. The presence and extent of residual invasive cancer at surgery is a strong prognostic factor for recurrence, particularly in triple-negative and HER2-positive disease. It converts that readout into a treatment decision: residual disease triggers post-neoadjuvant escalation. Moving chemotherapy before surgery has not been shown to improve survival. The EBCTCG neoadjuvant meta-analysis pooled patient-level data from ten randomised trials (4,756 women entered 1983–2002, median follow-up 9 years) comparing neoadjuvant chemotherapy with the identical adjuvant regimen. Breast-conserving therapy rose (65% vs 49%), 15-year local recurrence rose (21.4% vs 15.9%; RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.17–1.61, p=0.0001), and there was no significant difference in distant recurrence (RR 1.02, 0.92–1.14), breast cancer mortality (RR 1.06, 0.95–1.18) or all-cause mortality (RR 1.04, 0.94–1.15) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:27-39). The local-recurrence excess is not simply an artefact of good responders skipping surgery. It was largest in the two trials that permitted omission of surgery (10-year RR 1.62, 1.20–2.19) but persisted in the other eight, where surgery was scheduled irrespective of response (RR 1.28, 1.06–1.55), with no significant heterogeneity between the two sets (p=0.19). The evidence base is largely pre-taxane and pre-trastuzumab, which limits how far the local-control penalty carries into current practice. NSABP B-18 & B-27 is the founding randomisation. B-18 gave identical AC before or after surgery in operable disease (n=1,493 eligible): at 16 years neither overall survival (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.85–1.16, P=.90) nor disease-free survival (HR 0.93, 0.81–1.06, P=.27) differed, while preoperative therapy raised breast-conserving surgery (68% vs 60%, P=.001) (J Clin Oncol 2008;26:778-785). A significant treatment-by-age interaction for overall survival (P=.01) favoured preoperative timing under age 50 (HR 0.81, P=.06) and postoperative timing at 50 or older (HR 1.23, P=.07). B-27 then added preoperative docetaxel to AC. Pathological complete response doubled, from 13% to 26% (P<.001), with no improvement in disease-free survival (HR 0.92, 0.78–1.08, P=.29). Within both trials pCR was strongly prognostic (overall survival HR 0.32 in B-18 and 0.36 in B-27, both P<.0001). A doubled pCR that did not move survival is the first instance of the surrogacy gap the field still manages.

records.title: Patient selection
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Neoadjuvant therapy is mandatory in some patients and optional in others. Upfront inoperable disease: inflammatory breast cancer, and locally advanced stage III disease (bulky or matted cN2, cN3, or cT4). Operable triple-negative disease of T1c or greater (larger than 1 cm), and operable HER2-positive disease of cT2 or greater or cN-positive. These subtypes respond often enough for the readout to be informative, they receive systemic therapy in any case, and a non-pCR identifies a patient for post-neoadjuvant escalation. A large primary tumour relative to breast size in a patient who wants breast conservation. cN-positive disease likely to convert to cN0, which permits sentinel node surgery or targeted axillary dissection instead of axillary dissection, and more limited radiotherapy fields. A temporary contraindication to surgery, such as pregnancy, recent venous thromboembolism, or recent coronary stenting. For cT1 HER2-positive disease, upfront surgery followed by adjuvant treatment is preferred, since the pathological stage then allows systemic therapy to be de-escalated rather than over-delivered.

records.title: Work-up before starting
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Core biopsy of the breast with placement of an image-detectable clip, so the tumour bed can still be identified if the tumour responds completely. Axillary ultrasound in cN0 disease; ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration or core biopsy in cN-positive disease to confirm involvement. Clip placement in any pathologically involved node. Removing the marked node at post-neoadjuvant sentinel node biopsy lowered the false-negative rate of the procedure from 10.1% to 1.4% in a prospective study (JCO 2016). Breast ultrasound. Breast MRI is not routine but helps define disease extent, including multifocal and multicentric disease. Staging CT or PET is usually omitted in stage I–II disease, where the yield in an asymptomatic patient is low, and done routinely in stage III and inflammatory disease or where symptoms, signs or laboratory abnormalities suggest metastases.

records.title: Assessment on and after treatment
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Clinical examination before each cycle is the standard on-treatment assessment; imaging is repeated only if progression is suspected clinically or the surgeon needs it to plan the operation. Progression on neoadjuvant therapy is managed by proceeding to surgery if the disease remains operable, and by moving to the next line of chemotherapy if it does not. No imaging modality can exclude residual invasive disease, so the pathology of the surgical specimen is the only reliable readout. Axillary management after neoadjuvant therapy follows the pretreatment nodal status. cN0 before treatment: sentinel node biopsy at surgery. A negative sentinel node needs no further axillary treatment; a positive one is managed by axillary dissection, or alternatively by postoperative axillary radiotherapy. cN2–3 before treatment: axillary dissection. cN1 before treatment that remains ycN1: axillary dissection. cN1 before treatment that converts to ycN0: sentinel node biopsy with removal of the previously clipped node. Surgery, axillary staging and radiotherapy are covered in the early breast cancer chapter.

records.title: Pathological complete response as an endpoint
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: The definition used changes what pCR predicts. In the CTNeoBC pooled analysis , an FDA-led pooled analysis of 12 neoadjuvant trials (11,955 patients, all subtypes), clearing tumour from both breast and nodes (ypT0 ypN0 or ypT0/is ypN0) predicted overall survival better (HR 0.36 for both) than clearing the breast alone (ypT0/is, HR 0.51) (Lancet 2014;384:164-172). At patient level pCR is a powerful prognostic marker. Defined as ypT0/is ypN0 it predicted event-free survival (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.43–0.54) and overall survival (HR 0.36, 0.31–0.42), most strongly in triple-negative disease (event-free survival HR 0.24) and in HER2-positive, hormone-receptor-negative disease treated with trastuzumab (HR 0.15). At trial level it is not a validated surrogate. Larger between-arm pCR gains did not predict event-free survival gains (R²=0.03, 95% CI 0.00–0.25) or overall survival gains (R²=0.24, 0.00–0.70), far below the R² of approximately 0.75 conventionally required. A HER2-positive re-analysis (11 trials, 3,980 patients) reproduced the same split inside a single subtype: strong patient-level association (event-free survival OR 2.64, overall survival OR 3.15, with OR above 1 favouring pCR) and weak trial-level correlation (R² 0.23 for event-free survival, 0.02 for overall survival) (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2988-2997). A patient who achieves pCR therefore has a better prognosis than one who does not, but a regimen that produces more pCR is not thereby shown to save more lives. Response-adapted escalation is built on pCR; regimen selection is not settled by it. Residual Cancer Burden (Symmans) grades the non-pCR group that the pCR endpoint treats as one bin. In a pooled five-cohort single-institution validation (n=1,158, retrospective pathology review with prospective follow-up, not a randomised trial), the index was defined as continuous with predefined cut points of 1.36 and 3.28 (J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1049-1060). Ten-year relapse-free survival by class (pCR / RCB-I / II / III) was 86/81/55/23% in triple-negative disease and 95/77/47/21% in trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive disease. Two qualifications limit it. In HR-positive, HER2-negative disease the gradient was not monotonic (83/97/74/52%), with pCR itself entering the multivariable model as a paradoxical predictor (HR 5.03, 95% CI 1.60–15.78) on small numbers. In HER2-positive disease treated with chemotherapy alone it dropped out of the model, with RCB-II and RCB-III failing to separate (44% vs 47%). RCB index was independently prognostic in triple-negative (HR 1.92, 1.49–2.46) and trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive disease (HR 1.80, 1.26–2.59). It is prognostic only, and the authors call for external validation.

records.title: Triple-negative disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: The chemotherapy backbone and the carboplatin question Adding carboplatin to an anthracycline–taxane backbone raises pCR consistently; whether it improves survival depends on menopausal status. GeparSixto added weekly carboplatin (AUC 1.5) to paclitaxel and non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin over 18 weeks in the 315-patient triple-negative cohort. pCR (ypT0 ypN0) rose from 36.9% to 53.2% (P=0.005), and on the 2018 survival analysis 3-year disease-free survival improved (86.1% vs 75.8%, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.34–0.93, P=0.022), with the overall survival gain not significant (Lancet Oncol 2014;15:747-756; Ann Oncol 2018;29:2341-2347). Grade 3/4 neutropenia rose from 27% to 65%, and the homologous-recombination-deficiency score did not predict platinum benefit. CALGB 40603 (Alliance) , a 2×2 factorial randomised phase 2 (N=443) on weekly paclitaxel then dose-dense AC, found carboplatin raised pCR in breast and axilla (54% vs 41%, OR 1.71, P=0.003) but at 7.9-year median follow-up did not significantly improve event-free survival (HR 0.94) or overall survival (HR 1.12) (J Clin Oncol 2015;33:13-21; J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1323-1334). The trial was underpowered for survival, so this is an unproven rather than a disproven benefit. Within the same dataset pCR was strongly prognostic (5-year event-free survival 85.5% vs 56.6%), and even minimal residual disease at RCB-I fared worse than pCR. BrighTNess , a double-blind phase 3 (N=634) randomising 2:1:1 to paclitaxel plus carboplatin plus veliparib, paclitaxel plus carboplatin, or paclitaxel alone, each followed by AC, confirmed carboplatin's independent contribution (pCR 58% vs 31%) and showed veliparib added nothing (53% vs 58%, P=0.36), at grade 3/4 neutropenia of 56% and febrile neutropenia of 15% (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:497-509). At 4.5 years event-free survival favoured the carboplatin-containing arm (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.43–0.92, P=0.02), with no overall survival difference and no excess MDS or AML (Ann Oncol 2022;33:384-394). The TMC TNBC Platinum Trial (Gupta) is the phase 3 survival test (N=717, single centre). The primary endpoint of event-free survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03, P=0.081), while overall survival was nominally better (5-year 74.4% vs 66.8%, HR 0.74, P=0.029) and pCR higher (54.5% vs 40.3%) (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:9-19). A significant menopausal-status interaction confined the entire benefit to premenopausal patients (event-free survival HR 0.61, overall survival HR 0.57, pCR 61.7% vs 40.6%). Only the primary endpoint was alpha-controlled, so the overall survival and subgroup P-values are nominal. On this evidence platinum is supported in premenopausal triple-negative disease and argued against postmenopausally. The menopausal-status interaction comes from Gupta alone; the three earlier trials did not analyse it. The question is largely absorbed into current practice, since the chemo-immunotherapy backbone already contains carboplatin and its contribution cannot be isolated there. Chemo-immunotherapy KEYNOTE-522 is the standard for high-risk stage II–III triple-negative disease. In 1,174 patients it gave neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks with carboplatin–paclitaxel for 4 cycles, then with AC or EC for 4 cycles, then adjuvant pembrolizumab for 9 cycles, against the same chemotherapy with placebo (N Engl J Med 2020;382:810-821). Each link of the chain was formally tested against its own alpha boundary and cleared it. pCR 64.8% vs 51.2% in the first 602 patients randomised, a 13.6-point difference (95% CI 5.4–21.8), P<0.001 against a boundary of 0.003. Event-free survival at the fourth interim analysis, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.48–0.82), P<0.001 against a boundary of 0.01034 (N Engl J Med 2022;386:556-567). Overall survival at the final analysis (median follow-up 75.1 months), whole-period stratified log-rank P=0.002 against a boundary of 0.00503, with deaths in 14.7% vs 21.8% (N Engl J Med 2024;391:1981-1991). The 2020 publication states that its confidence intervals were not adjusted for multiplicity and cannot be used to infer effects. No overall survival hazard ratio is reported: the 5-year survival pair of 86.6% vs 81.7% is a descriptive landmark, and the weighted hazard ratio of 0.66 is an unstratified non-proportional-hazards sensitivity analysis carrying neither an interval nor a P-value. Benefit was consistent across all PD-L1 CPS strata on the 22C3 assay, which is the reverse of the same drug in advanced triple-negative disease, where the survival benefit is confined to CPS of 10 or more on the same assay. PD-L1 is therefore not tested to select immunotherapy in early disease. Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse events occurred in 13.0% vs 1.5%. Subgroups defined by outcome are exploratory, carry no alpha and were not tested against each other. In the no-pCR stratum event-free survival HR was 0.70 (95% CI 0.52–0.95), and by residual disease category 0.92 for RCB-1, 0.52 (0.32–0.82) for RCB-2 and 1.24 for RCB-3 (Ann Oncol 2024;35:429-436). Pembrolizumab was given before and after surgery with no arm stopping at surgery, so the neoadjuvant and adjuvant contributions cannot be separated. Two further trials bear on the regimen's edges. GeparNuevo (durvalumab) added neoadjuvant durvalumab to nab-paclitaxel then dose-dense EC in 174 patients, with no carboplatin and no adjuvant continuation. The pCR gain was modest and not significant (53.4% vs 44.2%, OR 1.45, P=0.287), yet at 86.4-month median follow-up durvalumab improved invasive disease-free survival (HR 0.56), distant disease-free survival (HR 0.41) and overall survival (HR 0.33), irrespective of pathological response (Ann Oncol 2019;30:1279-1288; J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1580-1586). It generalises checkpoint benefit to the anti-PD-L1 class, and being neoadjuvant-only it bears on whether the adjuvant phase is needed. As a phase 2 trial on a different backbone and antibody, it reopens that question rather than answering it. NeoPACT is a single-arm phase 2 (N=115, stage I–III) of pembrolizumab on an anthracycline-free carboplatin–docetaxel backbone for 6 cycles. pCR was 58% (95% CI 48–67) with RCB 0+1 in 69%, 3-year event-free survival 86% (98% with pCR vs 68% without), and grade 3 or higher immune-mediated events in 3.5% (JAMA Oncol 2024;10:227-235). There is no comparator, so no equivalence to the standard regimen follows from the cross-trial pCR similarity; SCARLET is the randomised test. Other checkpoint inhibitors have been tested on similar backbones with mixed results: Impassion031 reported pCR 58% vs 41% (a 17-point difference, p=0.0044), NeoTRIPaPDL1 67% vs 63% (p=0.48) against an event-free survival primary endpoint, GeparDouze 63% vs 57%, and CamRelief 56.8% vs 44.7% (a 12.2-point difference, p=0.004). GeparDouze (NSABP B-59), whose atezolizumab design closely modelled KEYNOTE-522, did not improve survival.

records.title: HER2-positive disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Establishing dual blockade Adding trastuzumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy improved pathological response and event-free survival in NOAH (pCR 43% vs 22%; 5-year event-free survival 58% vs 43%, HR 0.64, p=0.016), with a 5-year overall survival difference that did not reach significance (74% vs 63%, HR 0.66, p=0.055). NeoSphere brought dual blockade into the neoadjuvant setting. In 417 treatment-naive patients randomised to four cycles of one of four regimens, adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab plus docetaxel raised breast pCR from 29.0% (95% CI 20.6–38.5) to 45.8% (36.1–55.7), P=0.0141 (Lancet Oncol 2012;13:25-32). The chemotherapy-free dual-blockade arm still reached 16.8% and pertuzumab plus docetaxel 24.0%, so both drugs and the chemotherapy contribute. Grade 3 or higher events were mainly neutropenia and concentrated in the docetaxel arms. PEONY reproduced the pertuzumab effect in an Asian phase 3 (pCR 39% vs 22%; 5-year event-free survival 85% vs 74%, HR 0.53, p=0.027). Subcutaneous fixed-dose trastuzumab–pertuzumab is an option, shown pharmacokinetically non-inferior to the intravenous formulation in FeDeriCa (500 patients, stage II–III) with pCR of 60% in both arms. Paring down the chemotherapy backbone The de-escalation sequence has removed the anthracycline and then the carboplatin, while leaving the taxane in place. TRYPHAENA (N=225) was a three-arm cardiac safety study of dual blockade with FEC then docetaxel concurrently, sequentially, or with anthracycline-free docetaxel–carboplatin. Symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction was rare (2 patients during neoadjuvant treatment) and LVEF declines of 10 points or more to below 50% occurred in 3.9–5.6% across arms (Ann Oncol 2013;24:2278-2284). Descriptive pCR (ypT0/is) was high in every arm: 61.6%, 57.3% and 66.2%. TRAIN-2 tested the anthracycline directly in 438 patients with stage II–III disease. pCR in breast and axilla was identical (67% vs 68%, P=0.95) across every subgroup, and survival confirmed it (3-year event-free survival 92.7% vs 93.6%, HR 0.90, 0.50–1.63; overall survival 97.7% vs 98.2%) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:1630-1640; JAMA Oncol 2021;7:978-984). Toxicity favoured dropping the anthracycline: grade 3 or higher febrile neutropenia 10% vs 1% (P<0.0001), severe LVEF decline 7.7% vs 3.2% (P=0.04), and two acute leukaemias in the anthracycline arm. neoCARHP removed the carboplatin. In a phase 3 non-inferiority trial (N=774), six cycles of taxane plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab were non-inferior to the same regimen with carboplatin AUC 6 (pCR in breast and axilla 64.1% vs 65.9%, difference −1.8%, 95% CI −8.5 to 5.0, P for non-inferiority 0.0089), with fewer grade 3–4 adverse events (20.7% vs 34.6%) (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1587-1596). Non-inferiority rests on pCR alone; survival is immature. KRISTINE (TRIO-021) marks the floor. Replacing chemotherapy with T-DM1 plus pertuzumab cost 11 points of pCR in breast and axilla against docetaxel–carboplatin with dual blockade (44.4% vs 55.7%, difference −11.3%, 95% CI −20.5 to −2.0, P=0.016), despite far less toxicity (grade 3–4 adverse events 13% vs 64%) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:115-126). Event-free survival at 3 years was 94.2% with the chemotherapy regimen and 85.3% with T-DM1, driven by locoregional progression before surgery in the T-DM1 arm. The Neoadjuvant HER2+ therapy NMA (Villacampa) , a network meta-analysis of 46 randomised trials and 32 regimens (11,049 patients), supports most of that sequence and diverges on the last step: dual blockade plus chemotherapy was superior to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy for pCR, event-free survival and overall survival at the cost of more cardiotoxicity, and anthracycline-based chemotherapy was not more effective than anthracycline-free chemotherapy, but within anthracycline-free regimens carboplatin gave numerically better outcomes (Eur J Cancer 2023;190:112885). An antibody–drug conjugate front end DESTINY-Breast11 replaced dose-dense AC with four cycles of T-DXd before four cycles of paclitaxel with dual blockade, in 927 patients with high-risk disease (at least cT3 cN0, or cT0–4 cN1–3). T-DXd then THP improved pCR over dose-dense AC then THP (67.3% vs 56.3%, difference 11.2%, 95% CI 4.0–18.3, P=0.003), in both hormone-receptor-positive (61.4% vs 52.3%) and hormone-receptor-negative disease (83.1% vs 67.1%) (Ann Oncol 2026;37:166-179). The T-DXd-alone arm was closed early for inferiority (pCR 43.0%), so the taxane plus dual-blockade consolidation is still needed. Safety favoured the ADC front end: grade 3 or higher adverse events 37.5% vs 55.8%, all-grade left ventricular dysfunction 1.3% vs 6.1%, and drug-related interstitial lung disease low and similar across arms at approximately 4–5%. Grade 3 or higher interstitial lung disease occurred in 0.6%. Event-free survival is immature at 4.5% maturity (HR 0.56). Chemotherapy-free and response-adapted strategies A parallel line asks how little chemotherapy the lowest-risk patients need, using pCR to sort them. WSG-ADAPT-TP randomised 375 patients with HR-positive, HER2-positive disease to 12 weeks of T-DM1, T-DM1 plus endocrine therapy, or trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy. Despite higher pCR with the T-DM1 arms, 5-year invasive disease-free survival (88.9% / 85.3% / 84.6%) and overall survival (97.2% / 96.4% / 96.3%) did not differ detectably, on 46 events and 19 deaths in a trial not powered for survival, because non-pCR patients received mandatory standard chemotherapy (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3796-3804). Among the 117 patients with pCR, the 41 who omitted adjuvant chemotherapy had 5-year invasive disease-free survival of 92.1% against 93.0% in those who received it. WSG-TP-II compared 12 weeks of trastuzumab–pertuzumab plus endocrine therapy with trastuzumab–pertuzumab plus weekly paclitaxel in 207 patients with HR-positive, HER2-positive disease. pCR was far higher with paclitaxel (56.4% vs 23.7%; JAMA Oncol 2023;9:946-954), yet 5-year overall survival was 100% in the endocrine arm and 97.9% in the paclitaxel arm, untested, and the prespecified invasive disease-free endpoint was 92.1% vs 94.8% (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1974-1980). About 70% of the endocrine arm went on to receive adjuvant chemotherapy, so the chemotherapy-free label applies to the neoadjuvant phase only. PHERGain-2 took the strategy into node-negative disease. In 396 patients with centrally confirmed IHC 3+ tumours of 5–30 mm by MRI, eight cycles of trastuzumab–pertuzumab alone (with endocrine therapy if hormone-receptor-positive) produced pCR in 236 of 396 (59.6%), who then continued chemotherapy-free adjuvant dual blockade; 37.8% moved to T-DM1 and 1.8% to chemotherapy then T-DM1 (Ann Oncol 2026;37:837-848). Global quality of life declined by 10% or more at 1 year in 42.8%, and treatment-related adverse events occurred in 86.6% (5.6% grade 3 or higher), with one T-DM1-attributed death from pneumonitis. The 3-year recurrence-free interval co-primary endpoint is not yet reported. TRAIN-3 personalised duration rather than intensity, sending patients to surgery once MRI showed a complete radiological response. One third of hormone-receptor-negative and one sixth of hormone-receptor-positive patients reached pCR after only 3 cycles, and 3-year event-free survival was 92.2% and 92.0% respectively (Lancet Oncol 2026;27:349-360). Patients who needed only 1–3 cycles did better still (96.1% and 98.6%), but they entered that group by responding early on MRI, so this is favourable-prognosis selection rather than an effect of shorter treatment; no comparison between cycle groups is tested. Grade 3–4 adverse events and grade 2 or worse neuropathy rose with increasing cycle number, with no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: HR-positive, HER2-negative disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy here is chosen for downstaging rather than for its readout. pCR rates are low and its prognostic value is weaker: a meta-analysis (Spring et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020) found pCR associated with improved event-free survival in triple-negative and HER2-positive disease but only a trend towards significance in HR-positive disease. The neoadjuvant interval also allows time for germline BRCA testing to inform adjuvant treatment. Regimen selection follows adjuvant practice. Anthracycline-containing regimens are preferred, with docetaxel–cyclophosphamide as the alternative where anthracyclines are contraindicated. Either weekly paclitaxel or 3-weekly docetaxel, extrapolating from the adjuvant ECOG E1199 comparison. Either sequence, AC then taxane or taxane then AC, is acceptable. Neo-tAnGo, a 2×2 factorial phase 3, found a higher pCR when the taxane came first (20% vs 15%) and no role for added gemcitabine. Immunotherapy is under test in this subtype and is not FDA-approved for it. KEYNOTE-756 randomised 635 treatment-naive patients with grade 3, high-risk ER-positive, HER2-negative disease to pembrolizumab or placebo added to AC then taxane for 9 cycles, improving pCR from 15.6% to 24.3%, with event-free survival immature (Nature 2025).

records.title: Post-neoadjuvant therapy for residual disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Residual invasive disease at surgery identifies a high-risk patient and triggers escalation rather than observation. In HER2-positive disease, KATHERINE randomised 1,486 patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane and trastuzumab to 14 cycles of T-DM1 or trastuzumab. T-DM1 halved recurrence (3-year invasive disease-free survival 88.3% vs 77.0%, HR 0.50, 0.39–0.64, P<0.001) (N Engl J Med 2019;380:617-628). The final 8.4-year analysis sustained the gain (HR 0.54; 7-year invasive disease-free survival 80.8% vs 67.1%) and delivered a significant overall survival benefit (HR 0.66, 0.51–0.87, P=0.003; 7-year overall survival 89.1% vs 84.4%) (N Engl J Med 2025;392:249-257). Grade 3 or higher adverse events were commoner with T-DM1 (26.1% vs 15.7%: thrombocytopenia, transaminitis, neuropathy). DESTINY-Breast05 raised that bar for the highest-risk residual disease. In 1,635 patients with residual invasive disease who were node-positive at surgery or inoperable at diagnosis, post-neoadjuvant T-DXd cut invasive recurrence or death by about half against T-DM1 (events 6.2% vs 12.5%, HR 0.47, 0.34–0.66, P<0.001; 3-year invasive disease-free survival 92.4% vs 83.7%) (N Engl J Med 2026;394:845-857). The counterweight is pulmonary: adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 9.6% vs 1.6%, with two ILD deaths. Overall survival is immature. In triple-negative disease, CREATE-X (JBCRG-04) randomised 910 patients with HER2-negative residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline and taxane to eight cycles of capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 or to observation. Capecitabine improved 5-year disease-free survival (74.1% vs 67.6%, HR 0.70, P=0.01) and overall survival (89.2% vs 83.6%, HR 0.59, P=0.01) (N Engl J Med 2017;376:2147-2159). The benefit was concentrated in the triple-negative subset (disease-free survival HR 0.58, overall survival HR 0.52) and smaller and non-significant in hormone-receptor-positive disease (HR 0.81 and 0.73). The trial ran entirely in Japan and South Korea, which qualifies the effect size rather than the strategy. For germline BRCA1/2 carriers, OlympiA gave one year of adjuvant olaparib 300 mg twice daily against placebo in 1,836 patients with HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. Olaparib improved 3-year invasive disease-free survival (85.9% vs 77.1%, HR 0.58, P<0.001) and distant disease-free survival (HR 0.57), and at the second interim analysis delivered a significant overall survival benefit (4-year 89.8% vs 86.4%, HR 0.68, 98.5% CI 0.47–0.97, P=0.009) (N Engl J Med 2021;384:2394-2405; Ann Oncol 2022;33:1250-1268). Anaemia is the signature toxicity, with no excess MDS or AML. It enrolled both non-pCR patients and high-risk patients treated with upfront surgery, so it is response-directed-eligible rather than a residual-disease-only trial. Adjuvant pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-522 is a different kind of post-neoadjuvant therapy: it is given regardless of pathological response, so it is response-independent continuation rather than response-directed escalation, and its separate contribution was never tested. Sequencing these escalations is unresolved. A patient with triple-negative disease and residual disease after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy qualifies for adjuvant pembrolizumab, for capecitabine, and if germline BRCA-mutated for olaparib, and no trial has tested how to combine or sequence them. KEYNOTE-522 deliberately excluded adjuvant capecitabine, its design predating routine uptake of CREATE-X. Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition for high-risk HR-positive residual disease is covered in the early breast cancer chapter.
